question: Do generated locality exports and actual animal-atlas consumers preserve source-owned specimen chronology while presenting a locality hull only as display coverage?

normalization.preservation: All samples, refusals, ordered locality identities, memberships, coordinates, original text, date endpoints, mean, uncertainty/refusal metadata, individual support packets and all other bundle sections remain exactly unchanged. Both locality JSON and bundle locality records change only these three aggregate labels; CSV retains its31-column v2 schema and changes only corresponding three columns. No specimen identity/taxon/chronology decision, calibration, geometry replacement or new evidence.
normalization.output_scope: Build exactly one species bundle and render exactly three candidate files in fresh root artifacts. Do not invoke broad species/source-library/global materializers. No live product/data file is overwritten during producer or independent observer. Install only the independently verified three files afterward.

consumer_semantics.locality_visibility: An exact matched admitted original sample packet must satisfy the unchanged specimen chronology-publication predicate. A convincing aggregate hull alone is insufficient. Validate complete unique sample/support membership and exact source packet equality; only absent legacy support key permits source-packet fallback, never explicit empty/null or a locality hull.
consumer_semantics.display: Public locality chronology retains original display text and valid canonical navigation bounds, without claiming specimen dating basis/evidence/precision. Preserve explicit refusal reasons. Sample dates/provenance/conflicts/refusals remain literal and independently owned.
consumer_semantics.temporal_admission: Preserve generic structural/schema and explicit feature-level refusal checks. Then complete owned locality components take precedence over a merely contextual/unresolved aggregate posture. Occurrence filtering/indexing uses disjoint child intervals, never the hull gap. Invalid/missing/duplicate/unowned components, signed unsupported endpoints and individual refusals retain existing rejection semantics. Existing nonlocality and explicit signed-profile behavior is unchanged.
consumer_semantics.backend_browser: Python and the actual JavaScript temporal consumer must agree for positive, contextual, malformed, refused and gap cases. Correcting a draft negative-mean test must not change existing canonical endpoint/derived-mean behavior.
consumer_semantics.consequential_execution: After code and normalized-source qualification, execute the actual admitted animal locality consumer with complete supported/refused populations. Determine precisely which maintained outputs depend on the change before any further atlas materialization; reuse prior unrelated source/model/index qualifications without blindly repeating them.

input_guards.code: All tracked first-party Python bytes, HEAD, index and this protocol stable across producer and independent observer.
input_guards.data: Freeze the complete product animal-data/source-library tree because registry and receipt discovery participates in the builder, with exact before/after file inventories. Record actual opened scientific input identities and relevant repository pyproject files; no content/source substitution or private-bank copy.
input_guards.external_discovery: Preserve the actual BIJUX_POLLENOMICS_REFERENCE_STASH_ROOT resolution or existing fallback used by reference_stash.py; freeze the selected external directory/name/type inventory and resolution before/after, including absence. The reader uses name discovery, not these files as numeric contents. Never force a new empty stash to hide dependencies.
input_guards.network: No source acquisition or external message; unexpected network/source writes must refuse.

unsupported_claims: New dating or physical specimen identity
